classification: Verification-control lifecycle hardening, not an application defect
reasoning: invoke registers the new-session process group before tracking. Its new finally retires the group grant on success, nonzero child exit, exceptions, and cancellation after the wait/termination path. A reaped leader no longer leaves a numeric PGID authorized for later unrelated process adoption.

The grant retirement does not remove already attested PID/start descendants. track_processes and stop_owned_workers retain those identities and recheck start/command before termination. Subsequent live invocations acquire independent grants.

Five executed root tests use only fake Popen/process-table rows: immediate success/failure/cancellation retirement, reused-group rejection, and preservation of previously attested descendants. I reopened their assertions and raw output.

The tests do not execute Gradle or OS signals. Existing live-child timeout signaling and full OS race behavior are not newly runtime-proven by these five synthetic tests; the scoped group-retirement defect is deterministically covered.
